cleaned_devanagari_text:
प्रकरणम् १ ]    हिन्दी टीका सहित    ( ३ )

तृतीयामें द्वितीया-उक्त कर्म और गमनसम्बन्धी कृत्य, शिल्प, सीमन्त, चूडा, अन्नप्राशन, गृहकर्म[?] भी शुभ होते हैं । रिक्ता ४।९।१४ में अग्निकर्म, मारणकर्म, बन्धन, कृत्य, शस्त्र, विष, अग्निदाह, घात आदि विषयक कृत्य शुभ और मंगलकृत्य अशुभ होते हैं । पञ्चमीमें समस्त शुभकृत्य सिद्धि देते हैं, परन्तु ऋण (कर्जा) इसमें न देना; देनेसे नाश हो जाता है । षष्ठीमें तैलाभ्यंग, पितृकर्म और दन्तकाष्ठके विना सभी मंगल-पौष्टिक कर्म करने, तथा संग्रामोपयोगी शिल्प, वास्तु, भूषण, वस्त्र भी शुभ हैं । सप्तमीमें जो जो कृत्य द्वि॰ तृ॰ पं॰ ष॰[?] में कहे हैं वे सिद्ध होते हैं । अष्टमीमें रणोपयोगी कर्म, वास्तुकृत्य, शिल्प, राजकृत्य, लिखनेका काम, स्त्री, रत्न, भूषणकृत्य शुभ होते हैं । दशमीमें जो जो द्वि॰ तृ॰ पं॰ स॰ में कहे हैं वे सिद्ध होते हैं । एकादशीमें व्रत-उपवासादि समस्त धर्मकृत्य, देवताका उत्सव, वास्तुकर्म, सांग्रामिक कर्म, शिल्प शुभ होते हैं । द्वादशीमें समस्त स्थावर-जंगमके कर्म, पुष्टिकारक शुभकर्म सभी सिद्ध होते हैं । त्रयोदशीमें द्वि॰ तृ॰ पं॰ स॰ के उक्त कृत्य शुभदायक होते हैं । पूर्णिमामें यज्ञक्रिया, पौष्टिक, मङ्गल, संग्रामोपयोगी, वास्तुकर्म, विवाह, शिल्प, समस्तभूषणादि सिद्ध होते हैं । अमावास्यामें पितृकर्ममात्र होते हैं, कहीं शाबरोक्त उग्रकर्म भी कहे हैं । अन्य मंगल-पौष्टिकोत्सवादि कृत्य न करने ॥ ३ ॥ (अनुष्टुप्)

तिथीनां संज्ञा, सिद्धियोगाश्च
नन्दा च भद्रा च जया च रिक्ता पूर्णा तिथयोऽधममध्यशस्ताः ।
सितेऽसिते शस्तसमाधमाः स्युः सितज्ञभौमार्किगुरौ च सिद्धाः ॥ ४ ॥

तिथियोंकी तीन आवृत्तिमें नन्दादि पंच संज्ञा क्रमसे हैं, जैसे— १।६।११ । नन्दा,
content_en:
[ṭīkā] (commentary continuing on verse 3) On the third (tṛtīyā) the acts stated for the second, and acts connected with travel, craft-work (śilpa), sīmantonnayana, cūḍākarma (tonsure), annaprāśana and household work[?] are also auspicious. On the Riktā tithis (lunar days) — the 4th, 9th and 14th — acts involving fire, killing rites, binding, abhicāra (harming rites), weapons, poison, arson, striking and the like are auspicious, while festive and auspicious acts are inauspicious. On the fifth all auspicious acts succeed, but a loan must not be granted on it; granting one brings ruin. On the sixth, excepting oil-massage, rites for the ancestors (pitṛ-karma) and use of the tooth-stick, all festive and strengthening (pauṣṭika) acts may be performed; craft-work for war, building (vāstu), ornaments and garments are likewise auspicious. On the seventh, whatever acts are stated for the 2nd, 3rd, 5th and 6th[?] succeed. On the eighth, acts of war, building, craft-work, royal business, writing, matters concerning women, gems and ornaments are auspicious. On the tenth, whatever is stated for the 2nd, 3rd, 5th and 7th succeeds. On the eleventh all religious acts such as vows and fasts, festivals of the deities, building, martial acts and craft-work are auspicious. On the twelfth all acts concerning immovable and movable property, and all strengthening auspicious acts, succeed. On the thirteenth the acts stated for the 2nd, 3rd, 5th and 7th are auspicious. On the full-moon day sacrificial rites, strengthening rites, festive acts, acts for war, building, marriage, craft-work and all ornament-work succeed. On the new-moon day only rites for the ancestors are performed; in some places the fierce rites taught in the Śābara [tantra] are also mentioned. Other festive, strengthening and celebratory acts are not to be done. || 3 || (anuṣṭubh)

[Verse 4 — The names of the tithis, and the siddhi-yogas]
Nandā, Bhadrā, Jayā, Riktā and Pūrṇā [are the names of the tithis]. In the bright fortnight (sita) the [three successive rounds of] tithis are inferior, middling and excellent [respectively]; in the dark fortnight (asita) they are excellent, ordinary and inferior. And they are siddha (accomplishing, i.e. they form siddhi-yogas) on Śukra (Friday), Jña/Budha (Wednesday), Bhauma (Tuesday), Ārki/Śani (Saturday) and Guru (Thursday) respectively. || 4 ||

[ṭīkā] The five designations beginning with Nandā apply in order across the three rounds of the tithis, thus: 1, 6, 11 — Nandā; ...
ocr_review_note: ṭīkā, tṛtīyā clause: 'गृहमे' — expanded as गृहकर्म[?]; गृहारम्भ is an equally possible reading, the akṣaras after गृह are lost. ṭīkā, saptamī clause: 'व०' — read as ष॰ (ṣaṣṭhī)[?] by parallel with the daśamī/trayodaśī clauses, but the abbreviation letter is genuinely unclear. Separately (typo-obvious, corrected silently, not flagged): the verse number printed by OCR as '॥७॥' is ॥४॥ — confirmed by the ṭīkā closing '॥ ४ ॥' in the following chunk and by the verse sequence 3→5.

cleaned_devanagari_text: २।७।१२ । भद्रा, ३।८।१३ । जया, ४।९।१४ । रिक्ता, ५।१०।१५ । पूर्णा संज्ञक हैं । इनके जैसे नाम वैसे ही फल भी हैं । तथा शुक्लपक्षमें पूर्व त्रिभाग (प्रतिपदासे पंचमीपर्यन्त) अधम — अर्थात् इनमें चन्द्रमा क्षीण ही रहता है — द्वितीय त्रिभाग (पंचमीसे दशमीपर्यन्त) मध्यम और अंतिम त्रिभाग (दशमीसे पूर्णिमापर्यन्त) शुभ होते हैं; तथा कृष्णपक्षमें पू॰ त्रि॰ (पंचमीपर्यन्त) शुभ, म॰ त्रि॰ (पंचमीसे दशमीपर्यन्त) मध्यम और अं॰ त्रि॰ (एकादशीसे अमा॰ पर्यन्त) अधम होते हैं । चतुर्थपादका अर्थ यह है कि शुक्रवारके दिन नन्दा १।६।११, बुधको भद्रा २।७।१२, मंगलको जया ३।८।१३, शनिवारको रिक्ता ४।९।१४, गुरुवारके दिन पूर्णा ५।१०।१५ सिद्धि देनेवाली हैं । इसका प्रयोजन यह है कि "सिद्धा तिथिर्हन्ति समस्तदोषान्" इत्यादि — मासशून्य, मासदग्ध, दिनदग्ध आदि दोषोंको हटाकर कार्य सिद्ध कर देती है ॥ ४ ॥ (उपजाति)
content_en:
[ṭīkā] (commentary on verse 4, continued) — 2, 7, 12 are called Bhadrā; 3, 8, 13 Jayā; 4, 9, 14 Riktā; 5, 10, 15 Pūrṇā. Their effects correspond to their names. Further, in the bright fortnight (śukla pakṣa) the first third (from pratipadā up to pañcamī) is inferior — that is, in these the Moon still remains waned; the second third (from pañcamī up to daśamī) is middling; and the last third (from daśamī up to pūrṇimā) is auspicious. In the dark fortnight (kṛṣṇa pakṣa) the first third (up to pañcamī) is auspicious, the middle third (from pañcamī up to daśamī) middling, and the last third (from ekādaśī up to amāvāsyā) inferior.

The sense of the fourth pāda is this: on Friday, Nandā (1, 6, 11); on Wednesday, Bhadrā (2, 7, 12); on Tuesday, Jayā (3, 8, 13); on Saturday, Riktā (4, 9, 14); on Thursday, Pūrṇā (5, 10, 15) — these are the givers of siddhi (accomplishment). The purpose of this is [expressed in the maxim] "siddhā tithir hanti samasta-doṣān" — 'a siddha tithi (lunar day so combined with its vāra, weekday) destroys all doṣas (afflictions)' — that is, it removes doṣas such as māsa-śūnya (month-void), māsa-dagdha (month-burnt) and dina-dagdha (day-burnt), and brings the undertaking to accomplishment. || 4 || (upajāti)

( ४ )    मुहूर्तचिन्तामणि    [ शुभाशुभ-

रव्यादिवारेषु यथाक्रमनिषिद्धतिथिभानि
नन्दा भद्रा नन्दिकाख्या जया च रिक्ता भद्रा पूर्णसंज्ञा हताऽर्कात्[?] ।
याम्यं त्वाष्ट्रं वैश्वदेवं धनिष्ठाऽऽर्यम्णं ज्येष्ठाऽन्त्यं रवेर्दग्धभं[?] स्यात् ॥ ५ ॥

सूर्यादिवारोंमें नन्दादि उक्त तिथि क्रमसे अशुभ (घातक) होती हैं । जैसे रविवारको नन्दा १।६।११, सोमवारको भद्रा २।७।१२, मंगलको नन्दा १।६।११, बुधको जया ३।८।१३, गुरुवारको रिक्ता ४।९।१४, शुक्रवारको भद्रा २।७।१२, शनिवारको पूर्णा ५।१०।१५ । ऐसे ही नक्षत्र भी — जैसे रविवारको भरणी, सोमवारको चित्रा, मंगलको उत्तराषाढा, बुधको धनिष्ठा, गुरुवारको उत्तराफल्गुनी, शुक्रको ज्येष्ठा, शनिवारको रेवती दग्धनक्षत्र होते हैं । उक्त घातक तिथि तथा ये दग्धनक्षत्र शुभकृत्यमें वर्ज्य हैं ॥ ५ ॥ (शालिनीवृत्त)

तिथिचक्रम् ।
| तिथि | स्वामी | संज्ञा[?] | शुक्ल | कृष्ण | सिद्धि | [?] |
| १ | ... | नन्दा | अधम[?] | शुभ | ... | ... |
| २ | ब्रह्मा | ... | ... | ... | कार्यसाधन[?] | ... |
[ शेष सारणी पुनरुद्धार्य नहीं ]
content_en:
[Verse 5 — The tithis and nakṣatras prohibited, in order, on the vāras (weekdays) beginning with Sunday]
Nandā, Bhadrā, the one called Nandikā (i.e. Nandā again), Jayā, Riktā, Bhadrā, and the one named Pūrṇā — these are hata (struck down, destructive)[?] counting from Arka (Sunday). Yāmya (Bharaṇī), Tvāṣṭra (Citrā), Vaiśvadeva (Uttarāṣāḍhā), Dhaniṣṭhā, Āryamṇa (Uttaraphalgunī), Jyeṣṭhā and the last (Revatī) — these are the dagdha (burnt) nakṣatras (lunar mansions)[?] counting from Ravi (Sunday). || 5 ||

[ṭīkā] On the vāras beginning with Sunday the aforesaid tithis (lunar days), Nandā and the rest, are in order inauspicious (ghātaka, destructive). Thus: on Sunday Nandā (1, 6, 11); on Monday Bhadrā (2, 7, 12); on Tuesday Nandā (1, 6, 11); on Wednesday Jayā (3, 8, 13); on Thursday Riktā (4, 9, 14); on Friday Bhadrā (2, 7, 12); on Saturday Pūrṇā (5, 10, 15). In the same way the nakṣatras also: on Sunday Bharaṇī, on Monday Citrā, on Tuesday Uttarāṣāḍhā, on Wednesday Dhaniṣṭhā, on Thursday Uttaraphalgunī, on Friday Jyeṣṭhā, on Saturday Revatī are the dagdha (burnt) nakṣatras. The aforesaid destructive tithis and these dagdha nakṣatras are to be shunned in auspicious undertakings. || 5 || (śālinī metre)

[ṭīkā] Tithi-cakra (table of the tithis) — columns: tithi | lord | designation[?] | bright fortnight | dark fortnight | siddhi | [?]; first rows give Nandā — inferior[?] — auspicious ..., and for the second tithi Brahmā ... 'accomplishment of the undertaking'[?]. The remainder of the table is not recoverable from this scan.
ocr_review_note: Verse 5 pāda 2: OCR 'बृताकंत्' reconstructed as हताऽर्कात्[?] ('destructive, counting from Sunday') on the strength of the ṭīkā's gloss 'अशुभ (घातक)' and the śālinī syllable count; the printed akṣaras themselves are lost. Verse 5 pāda 4: OCR 'रवेदग्धम स्यात्' — रवेर्दग्धभं[?] adopted; रवेर्दग्धं is equally possible, one syllable is uncertain (the sense, 'the dagdha nakṣatras from Sunday onward', is secure from the ṭīkā). Tithi-cakra table at foot of page: column header 'सला' read as संज्ञा[?]; one header cell ('ओमि') is wholly illegible[?]; cell 'अम' read as अधम[?]; cell 'कार्य॑सायन' read as कार्यसाधन[?]. The table's grid is broken up by the OCR line order and most cells cannot be assigned to a row or column with confidence — the table is therefore rendered only as a skeleton, not reconstructed.

प्रकरणम् १ ]    हिन्दी टीका सहित    ( ५ )

क्रकचादिनिन्द्ययोगाः
षष्ठ्यादितिथयो मन्दाद्विलोमं प्रतिपद्बुधे ।
सप्तम्यर्केऽधमाः षष्ठ्याद्यमाश्च[?] रददावने ॥ ६ ॥

शनिवारसे विपरीत तथा षष्ठीसे सीधे क्रमसे गिननेमें, तथा प्रतिपदाको बुध, सप्तमीको रवि — अधम (शुभकार्यमें वर्जनीय) क्रकचयोग होता है । पंचांगोंमें इसे वारदग्ध लिखते हैं । इनकी सुगमता यह भी है कि, तिथि-वार जोड़नेसे १३ जिस दिन हों वही वा॰ द॰ । जैसे शनिवारकी षष्ठी, शुक्रकी सप्तमी, बृहस्पतिवारकी अष्टमी, बुधकी नवमी, मंगलकी दशमी, चंद्रवारकी एकादशी, रविवारकी द्वादशी; और बुधकी प्रतिपदा, रविकी सप्तमी — ये पृथक् २ ही कही हैं । और षष्ठी, प्रतिपदा, अमावस्याके दिन काष्ठविशेष नीम आदिसे दंतधावन (दातुन) न करना; किसी आचार्यके मतसे नवमी तथा रविवारको भी वर्जित है ॥ ६ ॥ (अनुष्टुप्) ।

कृत्यविशेषे निषिद्धतिथयः
षष्ठ्यष्टमीभूतविधुक्षयेषु नो सेवेत ना तैलं पलं क्षुरं रतम् ।
नाभ्यञ्जने विश्वदशाद्विके तिथौ धात्रीफलैः स्नानममाद्रिगोष्वसत् ॥ ७ ॥

षष्ठीके दिन तैलाभ्यंग, अष्टमीको मांसभोजन, चतुर्दशीको क्षौर, अमावस्याके दिन स्त्रीसंभोग मनुष्य न करे । किसीका मत है कि, मैथुन सभी पर्वदिनोंमें न करना — चतुर्दशी, कृष्णाष्टमी, अमावस्या, पूर्णिमा, सूर्यसंक्रांति ये पर्व होते हैं । उक्त कामोंमें तिथि तत्कालकी मानी जाती है, उदयव्यापिनी नहीं । तथा त्रयोदशी, दशमी, द्वितीयाके दिन तैलाभ्यंग (उबटन) न करना; यह नियम केवल मलापकर्षस्नानमात्रको ब्राह्मणरहित तीन वर्णोंको है । और अमावस्या, सप्तमी, नवमीको आमलेके चूर्णसे स्नान न करना — करनेसे धन एवं संतति क्षीण होती है; अन्य दिनों तिलकल्कसहित आमलेसे स्नान पुण्य देता है । यह वैद्यक शास्त्रसे भी स्नानकी औषधी वर्णकांतिकारक है ॥ ७ ॥ (इन्द्रवंशा) ।

दग्धादियोगचतुष्टयम्
content_en:
[Verse 6 — The reprehensible yogas beginning with Krakaca]
The tithis (lunar days) beginning with the sixth, [reckoned] in reverse order from Manda (Saturn, i.e. Saturday); and pratipadā (the first) on Budha (Wednesday) and saptamī (the seventh) on Arka (Sunday) — [these vāra-tithi combinations] are inferior [and form the Krakaca yoga]. And the sixth, the first and the amā (new-moon day)[?] [are prohibited] for tooth-cleaning. || 6 ||

[ṭīkā] Counting backwards from Saturday and forwards from the sixth [tithi], and further pratipadā on Wednesday and saptamī on Sunday, there arises the inferior Krakaca yoga (to be shunned in auspicious work). In the pañcāṅgas (almanacs) it is written as vāra-dagdha. An easy rule for these is also this: whichever day the tithi and the vāra (weekday), added together, come to 13, that day is vāra-dagdha. Thus: the sixth on Saturday, the seventh on Friday, the eighth on Thursday, the ninth on Wednesday, the tenth on Tuesday, the eleventh on Monday, the twelfth on Sunday; and pratipadā on Wednesday and saptamī on Sunday — these two are stated separately. Also, on the sixth, on pratipadā and on the new-moon day one should not clean the teeth with a particular wood such as nīm; in the opinion of some ācāryas the ninth and Sunday are prohibited as well. || 6 || (anuṣṭubh)

[Verse 7 — Tithis prohibited for particular acts]
On the sixth, the eighth, the bhūta (fourteenth) and the waning-away of the Moon (amāvāsyā, new moon), a man should not resort, respectively, to oil, meat, the razor and sexual union. Nor should anointing [with oil] be done on the viśva (thirteenth), the tenth and the second tithi; and bathing with dhātrī (āmalaka) fruits on the amā (new moon), the adri (seventh) and the go (ninth) is not good. || 7 ||

[ṭīkā] On the sixth a man should not take an oil-massage, on the eighth not eat meat, on the fourteenth not shave, on the new-moon day not have intercourse with a woman. Some hold that intercourse is to be avoided on all parvan days — the fourteenth, the dark-fortnight eighth, the new moon, the full moon and the solar saṃkrānti are the parvans. In these matters the tithi current at the actual moment is taken, not the one prevailing at sunrise. Further, on the thirteenth, tenth and second one should not take an oil-massage (ubṭan); this rule applies only to the mere cleansing bath, and to the three varṇas excluding the brāhmaṇa. And on the new moon, the seventh and the ninth one should not bathe with āmalaka powder — doing so diminishes wealth and progeny; on other days bathing with āmalaka together with sesame paste yields merit. By the medical śāstra too this bathing-drug is held to enhance complexion and lustre. || 7 || (indravaṃśā)

[ṭīkā] (continuing from the previous chunk) The sixth on Monday, the seventh on Tuesday, the eighth on Wednesday, the ninth on Thursday, the tenth on Friday, the eleventh on Saturday — these form the Hutāśana yoga. These three yogas give results answering to their names, and are prohibited in auspicious undertakings. || 8 || (indravajrā)

[Verse 9 — the Yamaghaṇṭa yoga, by vāra × nakṣatra]
On the vāras (weekdays) beginning with the Sun, the tithis[?] occur [as stated above]; [and now] Maghā, Viśākhā, Śiva (Ārdrā), Mūla, Vahni (Kṛttikā), Brāhma (Rohiṇī) and Kara (Hasta) — [these nakṣatras, taken] from Arka (Sunday) onward, are called Yamaghaṇṭaka[?]. They are to be shunned in auspicious work, and must without fail be avoided for setting out on a journey. || 9 ||

[ṭīkā] Maghā on Sunday, Viśākhā on Monday, Ārdrā on Tuesday, Mūla on Wednesday[?], Kṛttikā on Thursday[?], Rohiṇī on Friday[?], Hasta on Saturday — these form the Yamaghaṇṭa yoga. All these — Dagdha, the one called Viṣa, Hutāśana and Yamaghaṇṭa — are prohibited in auspicious work, and are especially to be avoided for a journey. For unavoidable undertakings their parihāra (remedial cancellation) is also given in other treatises: that the consideration [holds] chiefly [in the region of] the Vindhya range[?] ... and not in other countries; and further, if a benefic graha stands in a kendra or trikoṇa from the lagna, then their doṣa (affliction) does not apply. And some hold that only the 8 ghaṭīs of the Yamaghaṇṭa are to be avoided. Vasiṣṭha's view is that the four yogas give their evil result by day and not by night. || 9 || (upendra[vajrā])

Of Ūrjā (Kārttika), Āṣāḍha, Tapasya (Phālguna), Śukra (Jyeṣṭha) and Tapas (Māgha), in the dark fortnight [the void tithis are] śara (5), aṅga (6), andhi (4)[?] ... || 10 ||
Śakra (14) ... five, in the bright fortnight, śakra (14), adri (7), agni (3), viśva (13), rasa (6)[?], in order.

[ṭīkā] These are called the māsa-śūnya (month-void, also māsa-dagdha) tithis: of Bhādrapada [?], of Śrāvaṇa [?], ... of Vaiśākha [?], ... of Caitra [?] — these are void in both fortnights. Further, the 5th of Kārttika, the 6th of Āṣāḍha, the 4th of Phālguna, the 14th of Jyeṣṭha and the 5th of Māgha are void in the dark fortnight; and the 14th of Kārttika, the 7th of Āṣāḍha, the 3rd of Phālguna and the [?] of Jyeṣṭha are void in the bright fortnight.
